payload.name: Semiotic-informed digital health interface design
payload.fact: Redesigning digital health interfaces using semiotic-informed strategies increases symbolic comprehension, reduces cognitive load, and improves task completion rates.
payload.boundary: The study was evaluated with 30 heterogeneous participants aged 18-72.

provenance.title: From Signs to Systems: A Semiotic–Pragmatic Framework for Digital Health
provenance.quote_or_locus: Results indicate semiotic-informed redesign increased symbolic comprehension by 25%, reduced cognitive load by 39%, and improved task completion by 30

decision_note: REJECT, NOT_TRANSFERABLE, delegated by owner. The antecedent is a semiotic-pragmatic framework, not a variable: a design methodology applied to clinical health interfaces. A framework names no setting an interface can take, so there is nothing to act on even where the reported numbers hold.
